docs.title: CxxRelay
docs.text:
Bringing AI to existing C++ software.

CxxRelay connects established C++ applications to modern AI assistants without replacing their business logic. Register selected C++ capabilities, expose only approved operations, and execute AI-requested actions under host-controlled permissions.

  • Vision & User Story

    Understand the motivation, user experience, and real-world scenarios.

    Explore the vision

  • Developer Guide

    Build the project, register C++ methods, and run a local chat prototype.

    Get started

  • Technical Reference

    Explore the architectural boundaries, data model, security, and known limits.

    View the reference

docs.title: One framework, three responsibilities
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Existing C++ application] --> B[Reflection & invocation]
    B --> C[Authorized AI tools]
    C <--> D[Chat orchestrator]
    D <--> E[LLM provider]
    U[User interface] <--> D

Current project stage

CxxRelay is a working development prototype. Reflection, JSON, tool dispatching, chat orchestration, and local test UIs exist. The C API, MCP adapter, and reusable production GUI integration are planned.

Suggested starting point: Read the user story, then run the mock prototype.

Recommended workflow

Configure CMake in your IDE, select the prototype-* target, and run in mock mode first.

docs.title: Build without tests
docs.text:
cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF
cmake --build build --parallel

For Visual Studio or other multi-config generators, add --config Debug or --config Release to the build command.

docs.title: Run Catch2 through CTest
docs.text:
cmake -S . -B build-tests -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build-tests --parallel
ctest --test-dir build-tests --output-on-failure

Catch2 is a test framework for unit-tests. The buildsystem automatically download and build the framwork using CPM.

docs.title: CI strategy
docs.text:
Platform Compiler Main checks Linux GCC C++20 build, Catch2/CTest Linux Clang C++20 build, Catch2/CTest Windows MSVC C++20 build, Catch2/CTest

The CI workflow is separate from the documentation workflow. Interactive prototype-* targets must not be part of the normal CI build or CTest.

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text:
Symptom Check Python target fails Python 3 must be installed and discoverable at runtime. Windows UI does not launch Use Windows PowerShell 5.1 and STA mode; check the worker build. OpenAI mode rejected at configure time Model, API key, and libcurl transport must be available. Tool invocation rejected Confirm the method is exposed and the host grants permission.

Validation scope

The project contains C++ unit tests and a small mock-driven worker E2E suite. Passing these tests does not imply a live OpenAI integration or production deployment has been validated.

docs.title: Chat Prototypes
docs.text: CxxRelay ships two development interfaces backed by the same persistent C++ worker. The preferred workflow is to configure CMake once in your IDE and launch a custom target.

docs.title: Configure in CMake
docs.text:
Cache variable Default Meaning CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_MODE mock mock or openai (IDE dropdown) CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_API_KEY empty Optional key; prefer OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_MODEL empty Model identifier required for openai mode

Recommended first run

Use mock. It works offline, needs no credentials, and exercises the complete C++ tool-call workflow.

docs.title: Start in your IDE or terminal
docs.text:
Browser chat — all platformsWindows Forms — Windows only 
cmake --build build --target prototype-python

Requires Python 3; open http://127.0.0.1:8765/.

cmake --build build --config Debug --target prototype-powershell

Requires Windows PowerShell 5.1, but no Python or HTTP server.

The targets depend on prototype.worker, so the worker is built before the UI starts. On multi-configuration generators such as Visual Studio, select the appropriate --config.

docs.title: Live OpenAI mode
docs.text:
Set CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_MODE=openai and CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_MODEL to a model available to your API account. Make OPENAI_API_KEY available to both CMake configuration and the launched process.

API key handling

Avoid storing real keys in CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_API_KEY: CMake cache entries and generated build rules are not secret stores. The OpenAI adapter sends relevant conversation and tool data to the external provider; its current conversation continuation uses store: true.

docs.title: Fallback: start scripts directly
docs.text:
Linux / macOS browserWindows Forms 
<BUILD_DIR>/src/prototype/run.sh mock

# OpenAI mode
export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key'
export OPENAI_MODEL='your-model'
<BUILD_DIR>/src/prototype/run.sh openai

powershell.exe -NoProfile -STA -File .\start.ps1 -Mode mock

For OpenAI supply OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL in the environment.

The direct scripts are useful for troubleshooting; for routine development, prefer the CMake targets.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Register your classes → expose a tool → try the complete chat workflow.

docs.title: Register C++ Interfaces
docs.text: Existing structures and classes can be described without modifying their source definitions.

docs.title: Register fields
docs.text:
#include <cxxrelay/core.h>

using namespace CxxRelay;

// existing user-code
struct Point3D {
    double x{}, y{}, z{};
};

TypeRegistry registry;
registry.type<Point3D>("Point3D")
    .field("x", &Point3D::x)
    .field("y", &Point3D::y)
    .field("z", &Point3D::z);

Point3D point{1.0, 2.0, 3.0};
auto data = registry.to_value(point);
Point3D restored = registry.from_value<Point3D>(data);

The registry can also describe nested registered structures, std::vector<T>, and std::optional<T>.

docs.title: Register methods
docs.text:
// existing user-code
struct DocumentService {
    std::string search(std::string query) const {
        return "Found: " + query;
    }
};

registry.type<DocumentService>("DocumentService")
    .method("search", &DocumentService::search, {
        .parameter_names = {"query"},
        .description = "Search existing documents"
    });

A MethodDescriptor now carries the metadata needed to build schemas and perform controlled invocation.

Registration ≠ AI access

A method in TypeRegistry is not automatically available to an LLM. It must also be explicitly published through ToolDispatcher::expose().

Continue to tool calling.

docs.title: Expose AI Tools
docs.text: ToolDispatcher forms the authorization boundary between reflection metadata and an AI-requested function call.

docs.title: Publish a method
docs.text:
#include <cxxrelay/core.h>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

using namespace CxxRelay;

struct DocumentService {
    std::string search(std::string query) const {
        return "Found: " + query;
    }
};

TypeRegistry registry;
registry.type<DocumentService>("DocumentService")
    .method("search", &DocumentService::search, {
        .parameter_names = {"query"},
        .description = "Search documents"
    });

auto service = std::make_shared<DocumentService>();
ToolDispatcher tools(registry);
tools.expose("documents_search", service, "search");

ToolContext user{.principal = "demo", .allow_read = true};
ToolResult result = tools.dispatch(
    "documents_search", R"({"query":"Report"})", user);

The dispatcher validates JSON arguments, checks permissions, invokes the selected C++ method, and returns a structured result.

docs.title: Read and write operations
docs.text:
Operation Expected treatment Read-only May execute within the user's read permissions Write Requires write permission and host-side confirmation Unknown tool Rejected; registration alone is not enough Invalid arguments Rejected before method invocation

Never trust model-supplied authorization

ToolContext must be created by trusted application code. The model cannot grant itself permissions or approve a write operation.

For the end-to-end approval and continuation flow, see Chat and tool execution.

docs.title: Develop CxxRelay with Visual Studio
docs.text:
Visual Studio is the recommended workflow for developing CxxRelay on Windows. Open the CMake project directly, edit its settings in the IDE, and run the chat prototype without generating a separate .sln project.

  • Open the project

    Visual Studio loads the root CMakeLists.txt and discovers its targets.

  • Configure in the IDE

    Select a configuration and edit the CMake cache variables.

  • Automatic reconfiguration

    Saving CMake configuration changes refreshes the build model.

  • Run the native chat

    Build the prototype-powershell custom target to launch Windows Forms.

docs.title: 1. Open and configure
docs.text:
1. Install Visual Studio with the Desktop development with C++ workload and its CMake tools.
  2. Choose File → Open → Folder and select the CxxRelay repository root, containing CMakeLists.txt.
  3. Select a Windows x64 Debug configuration (or a suitable Configure Preset) in the toolbar.
  4. Let Visual Studio complete the initial CMake configuration. Its Output window shows the result.

No solution generation required

CxxRelay is a CMake project. Visual Studio handles configuration, builds, IntelliSense, and CMake target discovery directly.

docs.title: 2. Change prototype settings
docs.text:
CxxRelay exposes the following CMake cache variables:

Variable Value Purpose CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_MODE mock / openai Select the prototype provider; default: mock CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_API_KEY String, optional API key override; prefer an environment variable CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_MODEL String OpenAI model identifier, required in openai mode Recommended: CMake PresetsAlternative: CMake Settings

Use CMakePresets.json for configurations shared by the team and CMakeUserPresets.json for local overrides. The following is an optional example, not a required replacement for your existing presets:

CMakePresets.json
{
  "version": 3,
  "configurePresets": [
    {
      "name": "windows-mock",
      "displayName": "Windows · Mock",
      "generator": "Ninja",
      "binaryDir": "${sourceDir}/out/build/${presetName}",
      "cacheVariables": {
        "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "Debug",
        "BUILD_TESTING": "OFF",
        "CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_MODE": "mock"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Select the preset from Visual Studio's configuration dropdown. To use OpenAI, set CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_MODE to openai, specify CXXRELAY_PROTOTYPE_OPENAI_MODEL, and enable the project's optional HTTPS transport. Supply OPENAI_API_KEY through the environment.

When the project uses CMakeSettings.json, choose Manage Configurations from the configuration dropdown or right-click CMakeSettings.json and select Edit CMake Settings.

Edit the CMake variables for the active configuration and save the file. CMakeSettings.json and CMakePresets.json are alternative configuration mechanisms: Visual Studio does not combine them.

Keep API keys out of source control

Avoid placing real keys in CMakePresets.json, CMakeSettings.json, CMakeUserPresets.json, or CMakeCache.txt. The cache and generated build rules are not secret storage. Prefer the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable, available to the Visual Studio process during configure and when running the custom target. Never commit local credentials.

docs.title: 3. Automatic CMake reload
docs.text:
When you save CMakeLists.txt or the active CMake configuration file, Visual Studio normally reconfigures CMake automatically and refreshes its target model. The same applies when switching to a different Configure Preset.

The updated cache, compiler settings, and target list then become available to the IDE.

If a change is not picked up

Check Tools → Options → CMake → General to ensure automatic configuration is enabled. You can also invoke Project → Configure Cache (the exact label can vary with the Visual Studio version and presets mode). As a last resort, delete the CMake cache and reconfigure.

docs.title: 4. Build, run, and test
docs.text:
Windows Forms prototypeBrowser prototypeUnit tests
  1. Switch Solution Explorer to CMake Targets View.
  2. Locate prototype-powershell.
  3. Right-click the target and choose Build.
  4. The C++ worker is built as a dependency; the Windows Forms chat window then opens.

Start in mock mode first. No Python installation, HTTP server, or API key is required.

Build the prototype-python target in CMake Targets View. Python 3 is required; then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/.

Enable BUILD_TESTING=ON in the selected configuration. Reconfigure, build the tests, and run them using Test → Run CTests (or the equivalent test action in your Visual Studio version).

Custom targets versus debugger targets

The prototype-* targets launch interactive applications via CMake custom commands. Choose Build to execute them. Use F5 with an actual C++ executable target when you want to debug the worker itself.

docs.title: 5. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check No prototype targets appear Confirm the root CMakeLists.txt is open and CMake configuration succeeded Configuration changes have no effect Save the active preset/settings file; check the Output window and automatic configure options OpenAI mode is rejected Configure the model, API key environment, and optional HTTPS transport Windows Forms does not launch Use Windows PowerShell 5.1, check prototype-powershell, and inspect build output Tests cannot configure Install/discover Catch2 or use BUILD_TESTING=OFF for an initial prototype run

For other platforms or script-based fallbacks, see Chat Prototypes and Build & Test.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
CxxRelay separates describing, exposing, and executing existing application functionality.

flowchart TB
    GUI[Browser / Windows Forms / Host GUI]
    CHAT[ChatOrchestrator]
    LLM[ILLMProvider]
    DISPATCH[ToolDispatcher]
    META[TypeRegistry / descriptors]
    INV[Invoker / Value codecs]
    APP[Existing C++ services]
    GUI <--> CHAT
    CHAT <--> LLM
    CHAT <--> DISPATCH
    DISPATCH --> META
    DISPATCH --> INV
    INV --> APP

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text: Layer Contract Reflection Core Describe C++ types and methods independently of AI or UI. Value & JSON Convert supported structured data to and from transport values. ToolDispatcher Expose selected operations, validate input, enforce authorization. ChatOrchestrator Coordinate conversations, provider calls, tool results, and approval. ILLMProvider Abstract the AI provider; current implementation includes OpenAI Responses API. Prototype UI & worker Demonstrate a working end-to-end integration via JSON-Lines.

docs.title: Ownership boundaries
docs.text:
• The host application owns its domain rules, authenticated user context, and any database transaction boundaries.
  • The registry owns descriptors; services are shared through explicitly bound objects.
  • The LLM suggests calls but is never the authority for access rights or human confirmation.
  • The UI must dispatch callbacks to its UI thread; long-running operations should not block it.

A C interface is optional

The current integration calls C++ methods through the reflection layer. A stable C ABI or MCP interface can be added as an independent adapter, but neither is a finished component today.

docs.title: Chat Orchestration & IPC
docs.text: ChatOrchestrator coordinates model calls and tool results. The local prototypes place it inside a persistent C++ console worker.

docs.title: Conversation lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as User Interface
    participant Worker as C++ Worker
    participant Model as LLM Provider
    participant Tools as ToolDispatcher
    UI->>Worker: Send user message
    Worker->>Model: Prompt + tool definitions
    Model-->>Worker: Tool call + call ID
    Worker->>Tools: Dispatch authorized call
    alt Read tool
        Tools-->>Worker: Result
    else Write tool
        Worker-->>UI: Approval request
        UI->>Worker: Approve or reject
        Worker->>Tools: Continue if authorized
        Tools-->>Worker: Result / rejection
    end
    Worker->>Model: Tool result + call ID
    Model-->>Worker: Answer text
    Worker-->>UI: Streamed answer and completion

docs.title: Core interfaces
docs.text: Type Role ILLMProvider Synchronous completion API with optional text deltas. ChatOrchestrator::send() Process a new turn and required tool calls. ChatOrchestrator::resume() Resume an awaiting write approval with matching ID. ChatOrchestrator::reset() Start a fresh conversation after reset, error, or abort. std::stop_token Cooperative cancellation.

docs.title: Local worker protocol
docs.text:
The browser bridge and Windows Forms script communicate with the worker using one JSON message per line on standard input/output. The UI receives events such as text delta, requested tools, approvals, and completion messages. This is a prototype-specific protocol, not a published versioned IPC standard.

Runtime limits

The orchestrator limits tool/model loops and message size. A synchronous C++ function cannot be forcibly stopped by std::stop_token; domain functions must cooperate with cancellation when needed.

The current OpenAI adapter uses the Responses API with previous_response_id and store: true. Live provider behavior requires validation with actual credentials and the target model.

docs.title: JSON & Schema
docs.text: Value is the intermediate form between C++ objects, JSON data, and AI tools.

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text:
#include <cxxrelay/json.h>

using namespace CxxRelay;

Value request = parse_json(R"({"query":"report"})");
std::string encoded = to_json(request);

The parser and writer handle nested arrays and objects and preserve supported 64-bit integer values within the C++ process.

docs.title: Method argument schemas
docs.text:
Registered parameter metadata can be expressed as JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12). For example:

{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": { "type": "string" }
  },
  "required": ["query"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}

Schemas support structured and nested registered types via definitions and references. std::optional<T> currently maps to a nullable value, not an omitted property.

Schema is not the only validation step

The dispatcher validates the supported argument shapes and the invoker performs the final C++ conversion. CxxRelay does not currently implement a general-purpose validator for every JSON Schema keyword.

Large integers in JavaScript

Browser Number values cannot represent every 64-bit integer exactly. For large identifiers, use an explicitly designed string-based contract where required.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Component Purpose Value Owning representation of null, Boolean, signed/unsigned 64-bit numbers, double, text, arrays, and objects. TypeRegistry Registry of explicitly described C++ types and methods. TypeDescriptor / FieldDescriptor Names, type metadata, and registered fields. MethodDescriptor / ParameterDescriptor Method signatures, parameter ordering, and method metadata. TypeShape Transport-neutral description of structured types for codecs and schemas. Invocation adapters Convert Value arguments to typed C++ calls and results back to Value.

docs.title: Typical conversion
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CPP[C++ object] --> REG[TypeRegistry]
    REG --> VAL[Value]
    VAL --> JSON[JSON]
    JSON --> VAL2[Value]
    VAL2 --> REG2[TypeRegistry]
    REG2 --> CPP2[C++ object]

docs.title: Design constraints
docs.text:
• Registration is explicit, not automatic full C++ language reflection. But with C++26 reflection there will many other possibilities.
  • Value owns transportable data; it does not manage the lifetime of arbitrary live C++ objects.
  • The current invoker accepts value-like arguments and const T&/T&& via decoded temporaries. Mutable T& parameters are not supported for transport invocation.
  • Overloaded methods require explicit signature selection when their name is ambiguous.
  • const and noexcept qualifiers are described, but C++ type qualifiers are not equivalent to application authorization policy.

No automatic rollback

If an invoked C++ method modifies state before throwing, CxxRelay does not reverse that modification. Implement transactional behavior in the host application.

docs.title: Implemented in the current prototype
docs.text: Capability Status Value representation and type/field reflection Implemented Method descriptors and dynamic invocation Implemented JSON conversion and schema generation Implemented Allowlisted tool dispatch with permissions Implemented Chat orchestration, continuation, approvals Implemented Provider-independent API and OpenAI adapter Implemented; live API not verified here Local browser UI and native Windows Forms UI Development prototypes Cross-platform CMake and CI workflow Development workflow available

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• A reusable, non-blocking GUI adapter for the host application's UI framework.
  • A stable and documented C ABI for language-neutral interop.
  • An optional MCP adapter.
  • Stronger session isolation, host transactions, durable audit, and deployment controls.

docs.title: Tool Security
docs.text: Trust boundary: The model is an untrusted caller. ToolDispatcher applies host-defined rules before any registered method is executed.

docs.title: Authorization sequence
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    CALL[Requested tool call] --> KNOWN{Explicitly exposed?}
    KNOWN -->|No| REJECT[Reject]
    KNOWN -->|Yes| VALID{Arguments valid?}
    VALID -->|No| REJECT
    VALID -->|Yes| PERM{Host permits access?}
    PERM -->|No| REJECT
    PERM -->|Yes| WRITE{Write operation?}
    WRITE -->|No| REJECT
    WRITE -->|Yes| APPROVE{Human approval?}
    APPROVE -->|No| REJECT
    APPROVE -->|Yes| RECHECK[Recheck authorization]
    RECHECK --> EXEC[Invoke C++ method]

docs.title: Safeguards
docs.text:
Safeguard Current behavior Tool allowlist Only expose()d methods can be called. Access context Host-supplied ToolContext holds principal and read/write access. Per-tool ACL Optional tool-level authorization callback. Write confirmation Orchestrator pauses and requires an explicit host decision. Argument checks JSON/shape validation and typed conversion before invocation. Error handling Stable, sanitized errors are returned to external callers. Audit Optional callback, not a substitute for durable host logging.

Do not implement auto-approval

Never derive permissions or an approval response from model text or tool arguments. Display the exact immutable operation to the real user and collect a trusted decision.

Production deployment also requires identity management, isolation, rate limits, transactions, privacy review, and operational monitoring from the host application.

docs.title: Vision & User Story
docs.text:
Preserve proven software. Make its capabilities accessible to AI.

Long-lived C++ applications often embody specialized knowledge and mature business rules. Rewriting them to add a conversational interface is expensive and risky. CxxRelay provides an integration layer between those applications and AI systems.

  • User story

    Who benefits, what they need, and what success means.

    Read the story

  • Use cases

    Search, inspect, and update application data with controlled actions.

    Explore scenarios

docs.title: Guiding principles
docs.text:
Principle Meaning Reuse Keep established algorithms and domain rules in C++. Explicit exposure Reflection does not automatically make functions callable by AI. Human control Permissions and write approvals belong to the application. Provider independence Application interfaces are not tied to a single LLM. Incremental adoption Start with a small set of read-only functions and expand safely.

The idea

The AI can suggest an action. Only the host application decides whether and how that action is executed.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
These examples illustrate what CxxRelay enables; they do not imply that CxxRelay ships a document database or other application-specific services.

  • Find information

    "Show the documents related to the annual report."

    The assistant invokes an explicitly exposed read-only search method and summarizes the result.

  • Modify data

    "Rename this document to Final Report."

    CxxRelay checks permissions and asks the user to approve the exact proposed operation.

  • Explore engineering objects

    "Which nodes belong to this model?"

    Registered object metadata and application-specific query methods make structured data accessible.

  • Extend legacy software

    Add a conversational entry point while the original GUI and business logic continue to operate.

docs.title: A realistic adoption path
docs.text:
1. Expose one useful read-only method.
  2. Test it with the local mock chat.
  3. Add structured inputs and outputs.
  4. Enable sensitive operations only with the appropriate host authorization and confirmation.
  5. Integrate the workflow into the actual application GUI.

For a working starting point, see the Developer Guide.

docs.title: User Story
docs.text: As a developer maintaining an existing C++ application, I want to expose selected objects, data, and operations to an AI assistant, so that users can work with the application through natural language without rewriting the underlying code.

docs.title: A typical interaction
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as Chat UI
    participant AI as AI assistant
    participant Relay as CxxRelay
    participant App as C++ application
    User->>UI: "Find documents named Report"
    UI->>AI: User request and allowed tool definitions
    AI-->>Relay: documents_search(query="Report")
    Relay->>App: search("Report")
    App-->>Relay: Matching documents
    Relay-->>AI: Structured result
    AI-->>UI: Natural-language answer
    UI-->>User: Matching documents

docs.title: Extending the same conversation
docs.text: When the user asks to rename a document, the assistant can propose the corresponding tool call. A trusted UI requests approval before the write is executed. Declining the request leaves the operation unexecuted.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Selected C++ types and methods can be registered.
  • Methods can be exported as explicitly named AI tools.
  • Arguments and results can cross a JSON boundary.
  • Access rights are checked before execution.
  • The chat workflow can pause for write approval.
  • Local browser and Windows Forms prototypes demonstrate the workflow.
  • A production-ready, reusable GUI integration is available.
  • Stable C ABI and MCP integration are provided.
  • Make use of C++26 Reflection.

Value delivered

Existing functionality remains the source of truth; the assistant becomes an additional way to reach it.
